ranking.ranking_logic:
The ordering is driven first by selectivity-handle quality (does the warhead itself or a credible pocket confer selectivity), then lane openness, then validation depth and mechanism credibility — exactly the requested weighting, with selectivity and open-lane treated as the fundable/un-fundable separator.

Tier 1 (fundable, unique/credible selectivity + open lane): SLC1A5 sits clearly at #1 and ROSE most under equal-depth analysis — it is the only target whose covalent warhead is intrinsically family-selective (Cys467 is unique to SLC1A5; paralogs carry non-nucleophilic Thr/Arg). That is the single most valuable feature in covalent drug discovery and no other target here has it. Its efficacy/redundancy risk is real but is a biology risk, not a chemistry-feasibility or selectivity risk. PPARD (#2) is the highest-confidence call in the set: conserved warhead but selectivity already DEMONSTRATED via the non-covalent scaffold (GSK3787 has no measurable PPARa/g affinity), an empty covalent-antagonist lane, and high-confidence validation — its only true gate is indication/directionality, which is a strategic choice rather than a feasibility unknown. USP35 (#3) is a genuinely untouched lane with the USP30 precedent de-risking the pocket-selectivity playbook; it ranks below PPARD only because its validation is softer and more diffuse.

The decisive reshuffle vs the prior shallow ranking: RAF1 and IRF4 were co-leading, and equal-depth analysis demoted BOTH. RAF1 FELL hardest — to #6/WEAK — because its handle (C424) is computational-only with no ABPP evidence, is a hinge GK+3 cysteine (productively labeled in only ~1/124 covalent kinase inhibitors), and is conserved across the entire RAF/KSR clade, making it intrinsically pan-RAF; the field's own covalent-RAF work deliberately avoids this exact cysteine. Strong target validation could not rescue a conserved, possibly-non-ligandable handle. IRF4 fell more gently — to #4 but staying POSSIBLE_BIC — because its validation is genuinely top-tier, but the only characterized cysteine (C99) is pan-IRF conserved and the proposed unique handles (C194/C250) have zero reactivity/ligandability data; the covalent thesis is real but unverified, so it cannot outrank targets with proven or demonstrated selectivity.

YES1 (#5) has arguably the best validation in the entire set, but it is held out of the top tier because its lane is CONTESTED by a clinically advanced reversible competitor and the cysteine gives zero discrimination vs SRC/FGR — selectivity must be fully engineered. The WEAK tier (RAF1, AKR1B1, PRKCG) all share conserved-liability cysteines; AKR1B1 is further sunk by negatively-de-risked validation (two registrational failures), and PRKCG by a false unique-cysteine premise plus a CNS-only indication constraint. PRKCQ is the lone DEAD: its handle does not exist on the actual sequence, and the only real cysteine is buried and pan-novel-PKC conserved.
ranking.takeaway: Equal-depth analysis cleanly separates the field on one axis above all others — does the covalent warhead get selectivity for free, or must it be engineered against close paralogs? SLC1A5 is the standout and the new #1: it is the rare target where the reactive cysteine is itself unique to the target, an intrinsic family selectivity filter no other target here possesses, leaving only a biology/efficacy question. The prior shallow co-leaders both fell once leveled: RAF1 dropped to WEAK because its handle is computational-only, hard-to-label, and conserved pan-RAF, and IRF4 slipped to #4 because its world-class validation rests on two uncharacterized cysteines while its only proven cysteine is pan-IRF. The honest read: validation depth and selectivity-handle quality are anti-correlated in this set — the best-validated targets (YES1, RAF1, IRF4, AKR1B1) mostly carry conserved or contested handles, while the cleanest handle (SLC1A5) carries the softest efficacy thesis — so the top of the list rewards feasibility-plus-open-lane (SLC1A5, PPARD, USP35) over raw biological pedigree.

deep.covalent_handle: Catalytic nucleophile Cys450 (full-length canonical isoform 1, UniProt Q9P2H5, 1018 aa; verified ACT_SITE Cys450 / His862, USP/peptidase-C19 domain spanning 441-926). Cys450 sits at the N-terminal edge of the USP catalytic cleft (active-site nucleophile), solvent-exposed at the base of the Ub-binding groove between thumb and palm subdomains. Reactivity is established functionally, not just predicted: USP35 is covalently captured in cells by Ub-C-terminal activity-based probes (Ub-propargylamide / TAT-HA-Ub-PA), confirming Cys450 is a labile, electrophile-reactive thiol with a depressed pKa (classic His-polarized DUB nucleophile). Crystallographically resolved as the C450S mutant in PDB 5TXK (1.84 A, USP35 372-residue construct = UniProt ~423-944, bound to ubiquitin; catalytic triad density visible). No directed small-molecule electrophile reported yet; precedent (USP30) shows a Ub-mimetic vector is the way in.
deep.handle_source: Structure (PDB 5TXK, USP35 C450S + Ub) + UniProt ACT_SITE annotation (Cys450/His862) + functional ABPP (cell-permeable Ub-PA / HA-Ub-VME DUB-ome probes covalently label USP35) + DUB mutagenesis (C450A/C450S abolishes activity). NOT a scout-fragment (KB02/KB05) hit — not found in CysDB/isoTOP-ABPP datasets surveyed; this is a directed-electrophile / Ub-mimetic warhead handle, not an opportunistic ligandable cysteine.
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE LIABILITY at the warhead level: Cys450 is the family-defining catalytic nucleophile, conserved across ALL ~56 human USP DUBs by definition. Closest paralog is USP38 (reciprocal best-paralog), which carries the identical catalytic Cys; the same conserved Cys is present in USP30 (Cys77), USP7 (Cys223), USP14, etc. A bare cysteine-reactive warhead would promiscuously hit the DUB-ome. HOWEVER, selectivity is achievable from the POCKET, not the warhead — the USP30 precedent (cyanopyrrolidine on catalytic Cys77, >40-DUB selectivity in cells) proves this. USP35 offers unusual pocket-level discriminators: (i) the catalytic domain alone is catalytically INACTIVE and requires a USP-internal insertion region + C-terminal domain for activity (non-canonical, USP35/USP38-specific architecture); (ii) USP35 is an obligate homodimer via its C-terminal domain; (iii) an N-terminal HEAT-repeat/membrane region anchors isoform 2 to the ER. Net: warhead = liability, but the surrounding USP35-unique architecture is a credible, if unproven, selectivity HANDLE that must be engineered around Cys450.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric covalent inhibition of Cys450 with a ubiquitin-mimetic/cyanopyrrolidine-class warhead occupying the S1/Ub C-terminal channel (direct USP30 analogy; most credible primary route)

Allosteric / dimer-interface or insertion-region trap: USP35 is an obligate C-terminal homodimer whose catalytic domain is inactive without the insertion+C-terminal region — a covalent ligand engaging a unique non-catalytic cysteine at the dimer or insertion interface could lock an inactive conformation and confer selectivity away from the conserved triad

Covalent degrader anchor: USP35's auto-deubiquitination/CHIP axis and ER-membrane localization make a covalent-recruiting or covalent-CRBN PROTAC plausible, using Cys450 (or a surface cysteine) as the target-side covalent anchor to convert weak engagement into durable degradation
deep.validation: Moderate-to-soft and entirely preclinical. USP35 is implicated across many tumor types via overexpression/knockdown-correlative studies — ER+ breast (stabilizes/activates ERa, endocrine-resistance), prostate (BRPF1/MVA metabolism), HCC (ABHD17C/PI3K-AKT), NSCLC (BIRC3, RRBP1; cisplatin response), colorectal (FUCA1, ID3 immune escape), ovarian (STING-suppression, cisplatin sensitization), plus NRF2 and Aurora B (mitosis) stabilization. Breadth of substrates is a double-edged sword: strong biological rationale but no single clean pharmacology axis and high polypharmacology/on-target-tox uncertainty. NO hard genetic dependency signal (not a selective DepMap common-essential hit in the data surveyed), NO chemical-probe validation, NO clinical de-risking for USP35 itself. Clinical de-risking is only BY ANALOGY: the DUB/USP covalent modality is clinically de-risked (Mission Therapeutics USP30 MTX652 completed Ph1, cleared for Ph2 in AKI; MTX325 in Parkinson's), but that is class precedent, not USP35 precedent.
deep.existing_covalent: None found for USP35 specifically. No published USP35 small-molecule inhibitor (covalent or non-covalent), no chemical probe, no PROTAC/degrader, and no patent naming USP35 as the inhibited target surfaced in searches (2018-2026). The only covalent engagers of USP35 are pan-DUB activity-based probes (Ub-PA/HA-Ub-VME), i.e. research tools, not drug programs. Class context (covalent active-site Cys DUB programs at other USPs): Mission Therapeutics USP30 (MTX652, cyanopyrrolidine on Cys77, Ph2-ready, 2023-2024); multiple USP7 covalent/non-covalent programs. USP35 itself is an untouched lane.
key_risks: Selectivity vs the DUB-ome: the warhead targets the universally conserved catalytic cysteine (USP38 and ~55 other USPs share it). Selectivity must come entirely from the pocket/insertion-region architecture, which is unproven for USP35 and is the make-or-break risk.

Soft/correlative validation with diffuse polypharmacology: USP35 stabilizes many oncoproteins across many tumor types but lacks a clean genetic dependency or defined patient-selection axis; mechanism of efficacy (and the on-target toxicity ceiling) is unclear, and there is no chemical-probe TPP yet.

Non-canonical, hard-to-drug enzymology: catalytic domain is inactive in isolation (requires insertion + C-terminal dimerization), USP35 is an obligate homodimer, and (iso2) is ER-membrane-anchored — complicating recombinant active-enzyme production, biochemical assay setup, and crystallography of an inhibited complex.
deep.first_experiment: Run a competitive activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) selectivity screen: incubate a directed Cys450 electrophile (start from the USP30 cyanopyrrolidine chemotype on a Ub-mimetic vector) with full DUB-ome lysate (e.g., SH-SY5Y or HEK) and compete the HA-Ub-VME/Ub-PA probe, reading covalent occupancy of USP35 vs all other endogenous DUBs (USP38, USP30, USP7) by gel/MS. This single experiment simultaneously confirms Cys450 is liganded by a drug-like electrophile (tractability) and quantifies the pan-DUB selectivity window (the decisive lane question) before any structure-based optimization. Pair with a USP35 C450A counter-construct to prove covalent-on-Cys450 dependence.

deep.covalent_handle: Cys467 (resolved, human SLC1A5 numbering). Location: substrate-binding cavity of the TRANSPORT (elevator) domain, immediately adjacent to the HP2 hairpin gate. Cryo-EM (eLife 2019, Garaeva; PDB 6MP6/6MPB; Nat Commun 2017 6GCT) places the Cys467 thiol pointing INTO the orthosteric pocket, at H-bond distance to donate a proton to the Gln substrate carbonyl — i.e. it lines the same cavity a substrate-mimetic ligand occupies, and gates the side "pocket B" (Asp460/Asp464, Phe393/Phe407, Val463/Val477, Ala433/Val436). Accessibility/reactivity is functionally PROVEN, not inferred: methyl-mercury inhibits WT ASCT2 but loses all activity on the C467A mutant, and DTE-mediated redox activation also disappears in C467A (Scalise et al., Int J Mol Sci 2018, PMC5877509) — Cys467 is a genuinely solvent-exposed, redox-sensing reactive thiol with a likely depressed pKa from the polar substrate pocket. NOT scout-fragment-detected: no CysDB/isoTOP-ABPP entry was found, so it needs a DIRECTED, substrate-mimetic electrophile (acrylamide/chloroacetamide on a proline/amino-acid scaffold) rather than a fragment screen hit. The cavity is intracellular-/gate-accessible depending on conformation (outward-open 6MP6 vs inward-open C467R mutant 6RVX), so warhead reach is conformation-state-dependent.
deep.handle_source: Structure + functional thiol-modification genetics. PDBs: 6MP6/6MPB (outward, +Gln, eLife 2019), 6GCT/6RVT/6RVX (Nat Commun 2017 / Canul-Tec; 6RVX = inward-open C467R+TBOA, 3.61 A). Reactivity handle from Scalise 2018 (PMC5877509) Cys-scanning mutagenesis: C467A abolishes methyl-Hg inhibition and DTE redox activation. Family conservation from eLife 2019 and Frontiers Cell Dev Biol 2018 (PMC6131531). No ABPP/CysDB record located.
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE SELECTIVITY HANDLE — this is the strongest feature of the target. Position 467 carries a cysteine ONLY in SLC1A5. Aligned paralogs at the structurally equivalent position: SLC1A4/ASCT1 = Thr459 (the single residue that distinguishes the two otherwise near-identical neutral-AA transporters; engineering T459C into ASCT1 transfers Cys-reagent sensitivity — eLife 2019); SLC1A1/EAAT3, SLC1A2/EAAT2, SLC1A3/EAAT1, SLC1A6/EAAT4, SLC1A7/EAAT5 = a CONSERVED bulky Arg (e.g. Arg447 in SLC1A3) that forms the substrate salt bridge in glutamate transporters. So a Cys467-directed electrophile cannot covalently hit any of the 6 SLC1 paralogs (Thr and Arg are non-nucleophilic at this site). The covalent warhead is itself the selectivity filter against the entire family — the rare ideal case. Residual selectivity risk is OFF-pathway promiscuity of the electrophile against unrelated reactive cysteines proteome-wide (the usual covalent liability), NOT against SLC1 relatives.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric covalent inhibition — primary route: a substrate-mimetic (proline/amino-acid-ester, cf. Schlessinger Lc-BPE/ERA-4 reversible scaffolds) bearing a mild Michael-acceptor or chloroacetamide to alkylate Cys467 in the binding cavity, locking the transporter and abolishing Gln/Glu antiport.

Conformational/elevator trap — because Cys467 sits on the mobile transport domain at the HP2 gate, a covalent adduct can freeze a specific elevator state (outward- or inward-locked), a mechanistically distinct and potentially more durable block than reversible competition.

Degrader anchor (secondary/speculative) — Cys467 could serve as the covalent ligand handle for a covalent-recruiting degrader, but TPD of a 10-TM polytopic plasma-membrane transporter is unproven; lower priority than direct inhibition.
deep.validation: Genetic validation is solid but chemical validation is contaminated. Pro: shRNA/CRISPR knockdown of SLC1A5 and the mitochondrial SLC1A5_var isoform reduces glutamine uptake, GSH/ATP, and tumor growth across TNBC, prostate, NSCLC, melanoma, pancreatic xenografts; anti-ASCT2 mAbs (KM4008/4012/4018, Kyowa) block glutamine-dependent tumor growth; SLC1A5_var (Cell Metab 2019, Yoo) is HIF-2a-driven and essential for PDAC growth. Modality precedent for the glutamine-metabolism axis is clinically de-risked at the pathway level by GLS1 inhibitor telaglenastat/CB-839 (Calithera) — well tolerated but monotherapy ORR <5%, signaling efficacy/combination risk for the whole node. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the most-cited 'ASCT2 inhibitor' V-9302's anti-tumor activity was subsequently shown to act through SNAT2/SLC38A2 and LAT1/SLC7A5, NOT ASCT2 (Bröer 2018), and response did not track ASCT2 expression — so much published 'ASCT2 pharmacology' is off-target artifact. No selective ASCT2 chemical probe has clean target deconvolution; no SLC1A5 inhibitor has entered the clinic.
deep.existing_covalent: None found. Every disclosed SLC1A5/ASCT2 small molecule is NON-COVALENT reversible competitive: Schlessinger/Grewer rational-design hydroxyproline biphenyl-ester scaffolds Lc-BPE and ERA-4 (Ki ~0.74-0.86 uM, PMC8449414, biorxiv 2020 stereospecific-inhibition; PDB-supported binding in the orthosteric pocket but no warhead); sulfonamide/sulfonic-ester scaffolds (PMC6400523); aminobutanoic-acid series for NSCLC (J Med Chem 2023); C118P (Cancers 2023, partly off-target/'induces degradation' indirectly); V-9302/AABA (off-target SNAT2/LAT1); WO2024010732 (small-molecule ASCT2 inhibitors, mechanism non-covalent). Antibody lane occupied by Kyowa (KM4012/cKM4012). No covalent, Cys467-targeted, or irreversible ASCT2 inhibitor in literature or patents as of mid-2026.
key_risks: Target-efficacy / functional-redundancy risk: glutamine import is buffered by SNAT1/2 (SLC38A1/2) and LAT1 (SLC7A5), and intracellular glutaminolysis (GLS1) showed weak monotherapy clinical signal (telaglenastat ORR <5%). Inhibiting ASCT2 alone may be compensated; the SLC1A5_var mitochondrial isoform may also need engaging. The whole-node validation is genetically real but pharmacologically unproven because the headline chemical tool (V-9302) was off-target.

Engagement/PK risk for a covalent transporter drug: Cys467 lines a polar substrate cavity gated by HP2 and is only fully accessible in specific elevator conformations (outward vs inward). A warhead must reach a buried, conformationally cycling thiol in a multipass membrane protein — covalent kinetics (kinact/Ki) and cell/membrane permeability are non-trivial, and proteome-wide off-target alkylation by the electrophile is the dominant covalent liability (selectivity vs SLC1 paralogs is, by contrast, intrinsically solved).

Tractability/structure-execution risk: most high-res ASCT2 structures use the C467R/C467S stabilizing mutant, so co-structures of a covalent adduct at the native Cys467 must be generated de novo; recombinant WT ASCT2 is reduction-sensitive and aggregation-prone, complicating biochemical kinact assays.
deep.first_experiment: Intact-protein covalent-engagement test on Cys467. Express/purify WT human SLC1A5 (and a C467A/C467S counter-construct) in nanodiscs or proteoliposomes; treat with a focused panel of substrate-mimetic electrophiles (proline/amino-acid scaffolds capped with acrylamide and chloroacetamide warheads) and read out (a) intact-mass LC/MS for a single +adduct on WT that is ABOLISHED in C467A — proving site-specific Cys467 labeling — and (b) functional kill via radiolabeled/MS Gln-uptake inhibition in proteoliposomes with washout-resistance to confirm irreversibility. Pass criterion: clean, mutant-dependent Cys467 adduct with measurable kinact/Ki and washout-resistant transport block. This single experiment simultaneously de-risks accessibility, covalent tractability, and on-target mechanism, and (run against ASCT1/EAAT counter-screens) confirms the family selectivity handle — directly addressing the V-9302 target-deconvolution failure that sank prior chemical validation.

deep.covalent_handle: Cys249 (UniProt Q03181, hPPARβ/δ LBD numbering) — the documented covalent residue. Structurally it sits BEHIND HELIX 3, in the narrow neck/interface between the buried orthosteric Ω-pocket and the AF-2 (H12/coactivator) pocket of the ligand-binding domain. It is not a catalytic/active-site residue (nuclear receptor, no catalysis) — it is a pocket-lining cysteine reachable by a head-group electrophile that threads the LBP. It is partially buried (lines an internal pocket, not solvent-exposed surface) but demonstrably reactive/nucleophilic in PPARβ/δ: GSK3787 forms a stable Cys249 5-CF3-2-pyridyl thioether (SNAr/sulfonyl-displacement chemistry), confirmed by mass spec. No measured pKa in the literature, but functional nucleophilicity is established (Kaupang & Hansen, PPAR Research 2020, call it 'demonstrably nucleophilic in PPARβ/δ and PPARγ'). Directed electrophile required — not a scout-fragment hit; it is engaged only when delivered on a pocket-binding ligand (sulfonyl-pyridine, chloroacetamide-type warheads), not by promiscuous fragments.
deep.handle_source: Literature directed-electrophile / structure-grounded: GSK3787 (Shearer et al., J Med Chem 2010, 53:1857) covalent MS mapping to Cys249; CC618 (Toth et al., 2015) same residue; GW9662/T0070907 cross-react at the orthologous conserved cysteine across all three PPARs (Leesnitzer et al., Biochemistry 2002). Structural framing from Kaupang & Hansen 'The PPAR Ω Pocket' review (PPAR Research 2020). PPARδ LBD crystallography extensive (PDB 3TKM GW0742, 3GZ9 full agonist, 3ET2, 3GWX fatty-acid series) — covalent Cys249 complex itself not deposited; warhead site inferred from MS + apo/agonist structures. NOT a CysDB/isoTOP-ABPP scout-fragment-detected handle — PPARD does not surface as a high-confidence ligandable cysteine in broad chemoproteomic datasets; the handle is target-directed.
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE FINDING — the prior handle note ('Cys249, PPARG-Cys313 analog') is exactly right, and that is a SELECTIVITY LIABILITY at the warhead level, not a handle. Cys249 IS the conserved orthosteric cysteine: it is directly orthologous to PPARγ Cys313 (=Cys285 in the older γ1 numbering) and PPARα Cys276. All three PPARs carry a reactive cysteine at this aligned position behind H3. A bare electrophile aimed here would cross-label PPARα and PPARγ (GW9662 indeed irreversibly modifies all three, just with 10–600x potency differences). HOWEVER — selectivity is achievable and has been demonstrated: GSK3787 has NO measurable affinity for PPARα or PPARγ despite hitting the conserved cysteine, because selectivity is encoded in the NON-COVALENT recognition portion that exploits the δ-specific shape/electrostatics of the LBP (PPARδ has the narrowest, most lipophilic pocket; residues like His323/His449/Thr289-equivalents differ). So: the residue is a liability (conserved across PPARA Cys276 / PPARD Cys249 / PPARG Cys313), but a δ-selective reversible scaffold + warhead can deliver net selectivity — selectivity must be ENGINEERED into the binder, never assumed from the cysteine.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric covalent antagonism — VALIDATED route: GSK3787/CC618 occupy the AF-2-adjacent neck via Cys249 thioether, locking the LBD in a conformation that blocks classical agonist head-group engagement of AF-2 (irreversible antagonist). This is the proven mechanism.

Allosteric/Ω-pocket trap — plausible: the conserved cysteine sits at the Ω-pocket/AF-2 interface; a covalent ligand extending into the alternate Ω-pocket could act as an inverse agonist stabilizing a corepressor-favoring conformation, distinct from pure orthosteric block (analogous to T0070907 inverse-agonist behavior in PPARγ).

Covalent degrader anchor — speculative but credible: Cys249 could serve as the covalent anchor point for a PPARδ-directed monovalent degrader or PROTAC, converting irreversible occupancy into target removal; no disclosed PPARD degrader exists, so this is open whitespace.
Dimer/coactivator-interface trap — weak: PPARδ functions as an obligate RXR heterodimer, but no covalent handle at the dimer or NR-box interface has been mapped; not a near-term route.
deep.validation: Strong receptor-level and disease validation overall, but DIRECTION-DEPENDENT. Agonism is heavily de-risked: seladelpar (Livdelzi, PPARδ-dominant agonist) received FDA accelerated approval Aug 2024 and conditional EU authorization 2025 for primary biliary cholangitis — proving PPARδ is druggable, on-target-modulatable, and clinically tolerable. For the INHIBITION direction relevant to a covalent antagonist: validation is genetic + pharmacological in oncology — PPARδ agonist GW501516 accelerates colorectal tumorigenesis in Apc-mutant mice while antagonist GSK3787 suppresses it (Wang et al.; pro-inhibition), PPARβ/δ implicated across cancer hallmarks (angiogenesis via PDGF/c-Kit/VEGF). Modality: small-molecule covalent is appropriate (nuclear-receptor LBP is classically ligandable). Clinical de-risking of the antagonist direction is ZERO — no PPARδ-selective antagonist has entered the clinic; GSK3787 remained a 2010 tool compound.
deep.existing_covalent: Sparse and stale — this defines the lane. Validated covalent PPARδ binders: (1) GSK3787 — GlaxoSmithKline, sulfonyl-pyridine, irreversible Cys249 antagonist, disclosed 2010 (Shearer et al.), NEVER advanced beyond chemical-probe status; (2) CC618 — academic (Toth/Schubert), 2015, same Cys249 thioether mechanism, tool compound only; (3) GW9662 / T0070907 — pan-PPAR covalent tools that hit the conserved cysteine but are PPARγ-preferring, not δ-selective. No company has a disclosed PPARD-selective COVALENT inhibitor/antagonist in preclinical or clinical development as of mid-2026; reviews explicitly note 'no clinical evidence for PPARδ-selective antagonists.' No PPARD covalent degrader disclosed. So: covalent-antagonist lane is essentially unoccupied since the original GSK tool.
key_risks: VALIDATION DIRECTIONALITY (dominant): the inhibit-PPARδ thesis is contested. Antagonist GSK3787 suppresses CRC tumorigenesis, BUT PPARδ knockdown has independently been shown to INCREASE VEGFA-mediated angiogenesis and accelerate colon cancer growth (and reduce bevacizumab sensitivity) — opposite-sign data. The disease rationale for an antagonist is not settled; pick the wrong indication and the mechanism backfires.

SELECTIVITY LIABILITY from a conserved warhead residue: Cys249 is orthologous to PPARα Cys276 and PPARγ Cys313. A naive electrophile cross-labels all three PPARs (off-target metabolic/cardiac/oncogenic consequences). Selectivity is achievable (GSK3787 proves it) but must be hard-won from the reversible recognition scaffold, adding med-chem burden and a real proteome-wide off-target screening obligation.

COMMERCIAL/INDICATION whitespace is empty for a reason: the entire approved/clinical PPARδ franchise is AGONIST (metabolic/liver/PBC). There is no precedented clinical path or biomarker package for a PPARδ antagonist, and the agonist safety signal does not transfer. First-in-class burden is high and the indication must be built from scratch.
deep.first_experiment: Selectivity-resolved covalent engagement triage: synthesize/acquire GSK3787 (and a clickable analog) and run quantitative cysteine chemoproteomics (TMT isoTOP-ABPP) head-to-head on PPARα/δ/γ LBDs plus a live-cell proteome, reading out fractional occupancy at the aligned cysteine (PPARα Cys276 / PPARδ Cys249 / PPARγ Cys313) and proteome-wide off-targets. This single experiment simultaneously (a) confirms Cys249 is covalently addressable with a directed electrophile in a cellular context, (b) quantifies the actual α/γ cross-reactivity ratio that determines whether a selective covalent antagonist is feasible, and (c) maps the off-target cysteine liability — the three things that gate the whole program. Pair with a PPARδ corepressor-recruitment / reporter assay to confirm functional antagonism, not just labeling.

deep.covalent_handle: The stated handle does not survive checking. In canonical full-length human PKCθ (UniProt Q04759-1, 706 aa) residue 303 = Val and 322 = Asp; in the alternate C2-domain isoform numbering 303 = Val / 322 = Tyr; residue 424 = Lys. NONE of 303/322/424 is a cysteine in any UniProt isoform, so "ligandable C303/C322" maps to no actual cysteine. The "V3 regulatory hinge" (~283-380, the disordered proline-rich linker between C1B and the kinase domain) is an intrinsically disordered, non-folded segment with no defined pocket — not a covalent-druggable site. The only literature-real candidate cysteine is the strictly conserved αC-helix cysteine (reported as "Cys-424" in the 1XJD/JBC kinase-domain construct numbering, occupying the His87-equivalent position in the canonical kinase fold). That cysteine is BURIED in an αC-helix↔activation-loop double-salt-bridge electrostatic network (it is the structural reason Thr538-P cannot make the canonical contact), i.e. low solvent accessibility, not a surface nucleophile. No measured pKa or scout-fragment hit for it was found. Net: there is no validated, accessible, scout-detected covalent cysteine for PKCθ; the conserved αC Cys would require a directed electrophile reaching a buried site, and the front-pocket/hinge ATP region has no cysteine at all (pocket lining = gatekeeper Met458, Leu386, Gly387, Val394, Lys409, Val422, Glu428, Tyr460).
deep.handle_source: Structure (PDB 1XJD, 2.0 A staurosporine complex; JBC 2004 catalytic-domain paper) + UniProt Q04759 sequence/feature table (positions resolved against canonical 706-aa and C2-isoform numbering). Front-pocket-Ncap-Cys kinome survey (J Med Chem 2022, PMC8812259) and kinome covalent-cysteine survey (J Med Chem 2017, PMC5493210) used to confirm PKCθ is NOT in the covalent-tractable-Cys kinase set. No CysDB/DrugMap scout-fragment hit for a specific PKCθ cysteine could be confirmed.
deep.selectivity: Decisive and negative for the only real cysteine. The conserved αC-helix cysteine that the structure literature flags is STRICTLY conserved across the novel PKC subfamily — the equivalent position carries the same cysteine in PKCδ (PRKCD), PKCε (PRKCE), and PKCη (PRKCH), and PKCθ's kinase domain is highly homologous to these paralogs. So an electrophile reaching that residue would be a selectivity LIABILITY (warhead hits the novel-PKC relatives), not a handle. There is no cysteine UNIQUE to PKCθ in or near the ATP pocket/hinge to exploit. This mirrors the recurring PKC-isoform selectivity failure (sotrastaurin hits PKCα/β/θ and >200 kinases incl. Lck). The aligned paralogs to name: PRKCD, PRKCE, PRKCH (novel PKCs) plus the conventional PKCα/β/γ for the broader ATP-site homology problem.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric ATP-site covalent inhibition: NOT viable as a covalent route — no cysteine lines the PKCθ ATP front pocket/hinge (gatekeeper Met458; pocket = Leu386/Gly387/Val394/Lys409/Val422/Glu428/Tyr460); PKCθ is absent from the front-pocket Ncap-Cys kinase set. Reversible ATP-site inhibition is possible but is the crowded, selectivity-cursed lane that already failed.

Allosteric / C1-DAG-site or V3-hinge interface trap: conceptually the most PKCθ-distinct surface (the proline-rich V3 controls immunological-synapse localization), but no defined pocket and no covalent cysteine demonstrated there — speculative, would need de novo electrophile discovery and a directed cysteine that does not exist at the noted positions.

Degrader anchor (PROTAC/molecular glue): plausible workaround that DECOUPLES from the covalent-handle problem — would reuse a reversible binder (e.g. sotrastaurin-class) as the warhead and gain selectivity from the degradation event rather than a cysteine. This is the only route where PKCθ tractability is real, but it is non-covalent by design, so it does not satisfy the covalent thesis.
deep.validation: Strong genetic/biological validation in T-cell autoimmunity: PKCθ-null mice are protected in antigen-induced arthritis, EAE, autoimmune myocarditis, and allograft rejection, with impaired Th17 differentiation but enhanced/spared Treg induction (a favorable therapeutic-window signal). Directionality (inhibition = immunosuppression) is correct for autoimmunity. Clinical de-risking is NEGATIVE on the modality axis: the most advanced agent, Novartis sotrastaurin/AEB071 (reversible ATP-competitive bisindolylmaleimide, pan-PKC), reached Ph I psoriasis and Ph II renal transplant but was non-selective (PKCα/β/θ + >200 kinases incl. Lck) and did not progress to approval; enzastaurin/ruboxistaurin are PKCβ-biased, not θ-selective. Note a directional caveat from oncology: cancer-associated PKCθ mutations are loss-of-function/tumor-suppressive (PMC11346454), so the validated indication must be autoimmune/transplant, not oncology.
deep.existing_covalent: None found. No covalent small-molecule PKCθ inhibitor, covalent fragment hit, or covalent degrader is reported in the literature, patents, or pipelines reviewed (2004-2026). All disclosed PKCθ chemical matter is reversible/ATP-competitive: Novartis sotrastaurin (AEB071, Ph I/II, stalled), Boehringer/Rigel-era diaminopyrimidine and imidazopyridinone series (patents), and the PKCβ-biased staurosporine analogs (enzastaurin, ruboxistaurin, midostaurin). The covalent lane is technically empty.
key_risks: HANDLE IS FICTITIOUS/MISMAPPED: the named C303/C322 are not cysteines in any UniProt PKCθ isoform (303=Val, 322=Asp/Tyr; 424=Lys); the V3 hinge is disordered with no pocket; the only real cysteine (conserved αC-helix Cys) is buried and not scout-accessible. There is no demonstrated covalent tractability.

SELECTIVITY IS UNWINNABLE COVALENTLY: the conserved αC cysteine is shared with PKCδ/ε/η, so a warhead is a pan-novel-PKC liability — exactly the failure mode (broad PKC + Lck) that sank sotrastaurin. No PKCθ-unique cysteine exists to confer selectivity.

MODALITY MISMATCH WITH VALIDATION: the validated indication is autoimmunity where reversible/degrader approaches already cover the biology; the covalent premise adds no differentiated mechanism and inherits PKC-isoform tox/selectivity risk. (Plus oncology directionality is inverted — PKCθ is loss-of-function in cancer.)
deep.first_experiment: Intact-protein covalent occupancy screen on recombinant PKCθ kinase domain (and full-length) by LC-MS: incubate with a scout chloroacetamide/acrylamide fragment panel and measure adduct stoichiometry and the labeled residue by tryptic LC-MS/MS. This single experiment decides everything — it will (a) reveal whether ANY cysteine is electrophile-accessible at all and identify its true residue number, killing or confirming the entire premise (the prior C303/C322 note is almost certainly wrong), and (b) if a hit is found, immediately counter-screen the same fragment against PKCδ/ε/η to test the conserved-Cys selectivity liability. If no kinase-domain cysteine labels, the covalent thesis is dead and effort should redirect to a degrader using a reversible binder.

deep.covalent_handle: C424 = the hinge GK+3 cysteine (gatekeeper T421, so T421+3 = C424). Sits in the ATP-site hinge of the kinase domain (residues ~340-618; ordered in apo/inhibitor structures e.g. PDB 3OMV). Structurally equivalent to BRAF C532 (gatekeeper T529, T529+3) — the prior handle note is CORRECT, confirmed by gatekeeper alignment. By homology to BRAF, the thiol is reactivity-enhanced/pKa-lowered (BRAF: K417 salt bridge + G534 backbone-amide H-bond to thiolate), but it is partly buried UNDER the hinge, which is the standard reason hinge GK+3 cysteines are hard to label. Solvent accessibility is marginal, not open like a P-loop or front-pocket Cys.
deep.handle_source: Computational only: identified by constant-pH MD titration + pocket/ligandability analysis in the JCIM 2023 ERK-pathway cysteinome paper (Analysis of the ERK Pathway Cysteinome, doi 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c00014; PubMed 37022803). NOT validated by experimental scout-fragment ABPP/chemoproteomics. No CysDB/isoTOP-ABPP liganded-Cys report for RAF1 C424 found. Structural context from KLIFS/PDB 3OMV (CRAF kinase domain). Requires a directed electrophile appended to a type II hinge binder (belvarafenib/GW5074 scaffolds proposed) — has not been demonstrated as a covalent adduct in any disclosed compound.
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE NEGATIVE — this residue is a selectivity LIABILITY, not a handle. The GK+3 hinge cysteine is CONSERVED across the entire RAF/KSR clade: ARAF C444, BRAF C532, RAF1/CRAF C424, plus KSR1 and KSR2 all carry a Cys at the homologous GK+3 hinge position (JCIM 2023 cysteinome). So a warhead at C424 would label all three RAF isoforms (and KSR pseudokinases) = an intrinsically pan-RAF electrophile, NOT RAF1-selective. Direct confirmation that experts treat it as non-selective: the only disclosed covalent RAF-isoform work (bioRxiv Dec 2025, 'covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor', acrylamide-trametinib TWG-07-148) deliberately AVOIDS the conserved hinge Cys and instead targets ARAF-unique Cys514 — whose aligned residue in CRAF is Asn553 (non-cysteine), i.e. they used a NON-conserved position to get isoform selectivity. Contrast/benchmark: FGFR4 C552 (also a GK+3 hinge Cys) IS a clean handle precisely because it is UNIQUE (FGFR1/2/3 have Tyr; only ~6-7 kinases kinome-wide share that exact Cys) — RAF1 C424 fails this uniqueness test within its own family.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric covalent inhibition at the ATP-site hinge (append electrophile to a type II RAF binder, e.g. belvarafenib/GW5074 scaffold, reaching C424) — viable in principle but pan-RAF, not RAF1-selective; also competes with high cellular ATP

Covalent degrader anchor — use the hinge Cys (or a non-conserved surface Cys) as a covalent recruiting handle on a RAF1-directed PROTAC/molecular glue; degradation is the field-preferred route for RAF1 because it also kills the kinase-independent scaffold function, but a CONSERVED-Cys anchor inherits the pan-RAF selectivity problem

Allosteric/dimer-interface or RBD-CRD covalent trap — RAF1 activity is dimer-driven; a covalent at a non-conserved interface/regulatory Cys (not C424) could trap the inactive/monomer state and sidestep the conservation liability — but no validated non-conserved liganded Cys has been mapped for this on RAF1
deep.validation: High target validation. RAF1/CRAF is a non-redundant, standalone vulnerability in KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (PMC12880662, 2025: RAF1 knockdown/degradation effective with no added benefit from co-targeting ARAF/EGFR/DDR1), and is genetically required for RAS-driven tumor initiation/maintenance (classic CRAF-dependency literature). Modality is largely de-risked at the pathway level: 8 FDA-approved RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK drugs, and multiple clinical PAN-RAF (non-covalent) agents — naporafenib (Erasca, Ph2/3, NRAS melanoma, FDA Fast Track), tovorafenib (approved, pLGG), belvarafenib (Roche-discontinued Q1-2024). Field is now pivoting to RAF1 DEGRADERS to capture the scaffold function. Clinical de-risking of a covalent RAF1 specifically: ZERO — no covalent RAF agent has ever been in the clinic.
deep.existing_covalent: No covalent RAF1 (or any covalent RAF) inhibitor disclosed in the clinic or as a characterized compound. All clinical/approved RAF agents are NON-covalent and merely H-bond to the hinge Cys backbone (naporafenib, tovorafenib, belvarafenib, sorafenib, LY3009120). The only covalent RAF-family chemistry on record is preclinical academic and points elsewhere: (a) JCIM 2023 cysteinome — a computational PROPOSAL only, no compound; (b) bioRxiv Dec 2025 TWG-07-148, a covalent acrylamide targeting ARAF-unique Cys514 (a MEK-interface-region Cys), explicitly NOT the RAF1 hinge Cys. So the covalent-RAF1 lane has no incumbent.
key_risks: SELECTIVITY (dominant): C424 is conserved across ARAF/BRAF/CRAF/KSR — a warhead here is intrinsically pan-RAF, defeating any RAF1-selective thesis and reintroducing the paradoxical-activation / wild-type-RAF toxicity that has dogged the class. Isoform selectivity must come from a NON-conserved position, not C424.

TRACTABILITY: hinge GK+3 cysteines are rarely productively labeled — only 1 of 124 covalent kinase inhibitors (BLU9931/FGFR4) hits a hinge Cys; C424 is sterically buried under the hinge and is computational-only (no scout-fragment/ABPP evidence it is actually ligandable in RAF1).

DIFFERENTIATION/LANE-vs-degraders: the validated way to drug RAF1 (kill the scaffold function) is degradation, and pan-RAF non-covalent inhibitors are already clinical — a covalent ATP-site inhibitor at a conserved Cys may be strictly worse than both, with no clear niche.
deep.first_experiment: Run an intact-protein LC-MS covalent-labeling assay on recombinant RAF1, ARAF and BRAF kinase domains in parallel with a directed-electrophile (acrylamide/chloroacetamide) analog of a type II hinge binder, then trypsin-digest to map the adduct. Two reads in one experiment: (1) does C424 actually get labeled at all (tractability — is the computational handle real)? and (2) the cross-isoform panel quantifies the predicted pan-RAF liability. If labeling is RAF-promiscuous (expected), the program must pivot to a NON-conserved Cys (e.g. a CRAF residue where ARAF/BRAF differ) or to a covalent degrader anchor — making this the single decisive go/no-go on the whole C424 thesis.

deep.covalent_handle: IRF4 (UniProt Q15306, 451 aa) has 5 cysteines: C17 (N-term), C99 (DBD, domain 21-129/20-134), C194 (compact folded linker, ~135-237), C250 (IAD edge, ~238+), C284 (IAD). The structurally characterized one is C99: it sits at the CENTER of the alpha3 DNA-recognition helix, immediately adjacent to the functional hotspot R98, and directly contacts the GAAA/IRE motif (PDB 7JM4 DBD homodimer; 8JKL/8JKQ DBD-DNA). C99 is reactive enough to form disulfide-linked dimers and C99A reduces DNA binding -> it is functional and at least partially solvent-accessible at the DNA interface, but its reactivity/pKa has NOT been measured by chemoproteomics. C194/C250 are the proposed selectivity handles but are UNCHARACTERIZED structurally for accessibility and have no published reactivity data; they would need a directed electrophile + structural/ABPP confirmation. No IRF4 cysteine was found as a scout-fragment hit in any surfaced CysDB/isoTOP-ABPP dataset.
deep.handle_source: Structure (PDB 7JM4 DBD homodimer/ISRE; 8JKL, 8JKQ DBD-DNA; 5BVI IAD) + UniProt Q15306 cysteine/domain annotation + literature (C99 functional/disulfide). NOT from a chemoproteomic scout-fragment hit — no IRF4 ABPP ligandability data surfaced (CysDB covers ~24% of cysteinome; IRF4 cysteines not reported as ligandable in results found).
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE AND MOSTLY NEGATIVE. C99 is a selectivity LIABILITY: it is conserved from human to zebrafish AND across the IRF family at the aligned alpha3-helix position in ALL paralogs except IRF3 (which has serine). Aligned paralogs carrying the equivalent cysteine include IRF1, IRF2, IRF5, IRF6, IRF7, IRF8, IRF9 — a C99-directed warhead would be expected to hit these, especially the close DBD homologs IRF8/IRF5 (DBD >115 aa homology across IRF1-9). A covalent IRF8/IRF5 DBD-cysteine degrader series already exists (bioRxiv 2025.08.03.668300), reinforcing that this position is cross-reactive across the family. C194 (compact linker) and C250 (IAD edge) are the only plausible IRF4-UNIQUE handles, because the C-terminal IAD/linker is the divergent region (IRF4 IAD loop 3/loop 5 differ from IRF3/IRF5), but their paralog uniqueness is INFERRED from IAD divergence, NOT confirmed by an explicit IRF1-9 alignment at those exact positions in the sources found. So: real handle (C99) = liability; claimed handles (C194/C250) = unverified.
mechanism_routes: Degrader anchor (most credible): covalent ligand at a unique linker/IAD cysteine (C194 or C250) as the warhead end of a CRBN/VHL PROTAC or molecular glue — extends the existing NON-covalent (S)-H1 -> dIRF4-2 IAD-binder PROTAC concept (Nat Chem Biol 2026) by adding covalency for residence/selectivity

Allosteric/interface trap: covalent wedge at C250 on the IAD edge to disrupt the IRF4-SPI1/PU.1 EICE interface (IAD residues K399/R398) or IAD homo/heterodimerization, blocking the transcriptional complex without needing a deep orthosteric pocket
Orthosteric DBD inhibition via C99 (LOW priority): chemically tractable cysteine at the DNA interface but pan-IRF cross-reactivity makes selective orthosteric inhibition very unlikely
deep.validation: VERY STRONG target validation. Genetic: Staudt 2008 Nature 'IRF4 addiction' — non-oncogene addiction in multiple myeloma; ~50% IRF4 knockdown kills MM lines regardless of driver, and irf4-haploinsufficient mice are normal => therapeutic window. C99R is a recurrent driver mutation in classic Hodgkin lymphoma (neomorphic DNA binding), adding disease causality. CLINICAL de-risking of IRF4 knockdown exists but via a DIFFERENT modality: Ionis ASO frenlosirsen/ION251 completed a Phase 1a dose-escalation in R/R MM with acceptable safety and molecular/efficacy signal (AACR abstract CT146, Apr 2025). No small-molecule (covalent or not) has reached the clinic; dIRF4-2 PROTAC and (S)-H1 binder are academic/preclinical.
deep.existing_covalent: No covalent small-molecule IRF4 program found (covalent lane is empty). Closest: (i) Ionis frenlosirsen/ION251 — IRF4 antisense oligonucleotide, Phase 1a R/R MM (AACR 2025), not a small molecule; (ii) (S)-H1, a NON-covalent IRF4 IAD binder hitting the SPI1/PU.1 interface, built into dIRF4-2, a first-in-class CRBN-based PROTAC degrader (academic/preclinical, Nat Chem Biol 2026, s41589-026-02228-8); (iii) bisnoralcohol/SH514-class non-covalent IRF4 inhibitors (preclinical, ~uM). Covalent precedent exists for SIBLING paralogs IRF8 and IRF5 (covalent degraders, bioRxiv 2025.08.03.668300) — relevant as both feasibility proof and a cross-reactivity warning for any conserved-cysteine approach.
key_risks: Selectivity at the only validated handle is bad: C99 is pan-IRF conserved (all paralogs except IRF3), so a C99 warhead risks hitting IRF8/IRF5/IRF1 etc. The proposed IRF4-unique handles (C194 linker, C250 IAD edge) have NO published ligandability or reactivity data and their paralog-uniqueness is inferred, not proven — the entire covalent thesis rests on two uncharacterized cysteines.

Ligandability/accessibility unknown: IRF4 is a transcription factor with shallow interfaces and a flexible autoinhibitory region; no chemoproteomic/ABPP hit on any IRF4 cysteine surfaced, the linker is compact (may bury C194), and DBD-only structures don't resolve the linker/IAD cysteine microenvironments — high chance C194/C250 are not productively engageable.

Modality competition and differentiation: IRF4 knockdown is already clinically de-risked by an ASO (frenlosirsen, Ph1a) and chased by a non-covalent IAD-binder PROTAC; a covalent small molecule must beat ASO/PROTAC on a real axis (oral exposure, depth/durability of degradation, selectivity) or it has no lane rationale.
deep.first_experiment: Run cysteine-reactive chemoproteomics on full-length recombinant IRF4 (and in MM cell lysate): intact-protein LC-MS plus competitive isoTOP-ABPP/label-free ABPP with an iodoacetamide-alkyne and a small covalent-fragment/scout panel, to (a) measure which of C99/C194/C250/C284 are actually reactive and ligandable, and (b) in parallel lysate ABPP, directly test paralog selectivity by quantifying co-engagement of IRF8/IRF5/IRF1 at the aligned C99-equivalent. Decision gate: a fragment that labels C194 or C250 with IRF4 selectivity over IRF8/IRF5 greenlights a covalent-degrader campaign; if only C99 is hit and it co-labels paralogs, the covalent thesis is dead and the program should default to the non-covalent IAD-binder/PROTAC route.

deep.covalent_handle: Cys287 in the glycine-rich phosphate-binding loop (P-loop / nucleotide-binding region res. 283–291) of the YES1 kinase domain, sitting at the roof of the ATP pocket. It is the structural equivalent of SRC Cys277 (the prior note's "C287/C277" are the SAME residue under two numbering conventions — full-length YES1 = 287, SRC kinase-domain numbering = 277; the SM1-71 paper's "C280" is yet another SRC isoform convention for the identical position, not a separate cysteine). It is partially solvent-accessible and ATP-pocket-proximal but NOT pre-organized for reaction: the P-loop must swing toward the warhead, giving slow covalent inactivation kinetics (documented for the SRC analog DGY-06-116). So it is a "conditionally reactive" P-loop cysteine, not a hyper-nucleophilic active-site cysteine. Reactivity/pKa not directly measured for YES1; behaves as a moderately reactive cysteine requiring a properly vectored acrylamide delivered off a high-affinity reversible scaffold.
deep.handle_source: Literature ABPP / chemoproteomics (Gray lab, Cell Chem Biol 2019, SM1-71 promiscuity screen: YES1 C287 >50% labeled at low-nM acrylamide; iodoacetamide-probe labeled in cysteine chemoproteomics datasets) + structural inference from SRC covalent co-crystals (DGY-06-116, PDB 6E6E; SM1-71–SRC PDB 6ATE). YES1's own kinase domain is crystallographically solved (apo/ATP-site structures exist) but no YES1–covalent-adduct co-crystal is published — the adduct geometry is borrowed from the SRC P-loop-cysteine structures.
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE AXIS — mixed, and this is the whole story. The C287 P-loop cysteine is NOT pan-kinase: only 9 human kinases carry an equivalently positioned P-loop cysteine — SRC (C277), YES1 (C287), FGR, FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, FGFR4, LIMK1, TNK1 (Brameld/Gray, J Med Chem 2020; Cell Chem Biol 2019). WITHIN the SRC-family (the paralogs that drive off-target tox), this is a partial SELECTIVITY FILTER: of the 8 SFKs (SRC, FYN, YES1, FGR, LYN, LCK, HCK, BLK), ONLY SRC, YES1, and FGR have the P-loop Cys — FYN, LYN, LCK, HCK, BLK have a non-Cys residue there and are excluded by the warhead. BUT it is a hard LIABILITY versus three relatives: (i) SRC C277 — ~88% kinase-domain identity, essentially the same pocket, so a YES1 covalent will hit SRC by default (the SRC-directed DGY-06-116 hits YES1 with low-nM IC50, proving the reciprocal); (ii) FGR; and (iii) the FGFR1-4 cluster — clinically proven cross-reactive: the approved FGFR drug futibatinib (TAS-120), which covalently caps the FGFR P-loop cysteine, forms covalent adducts on SRC/YES off-target. Net: the warhead alone CANNOT distinguish YES1 from SRC/FGR/FGFR — selectivity must be engineered entirely from the reversible scaffold (gatekeeper Thr338-equiv, back hydrophobic pocket, hinge). The cysteine is a reactivity enabler, not the selectivity determinant.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric ATP-competitive covalent inhibition — anchor a reversible ATP-site scaffold (dasatinib/eCF506-like) and vector an acrylamide onto C287; precedented by DGY-06-116 on the SRC paralog (PDB 6E6E). Most direct route.

Covalent conformation-trap (Type 1.5) — combine the eCF506/NXP900 'closed-conformation lock' pharmacology (inhibits BOTH catalytic AND scaffolding/SH2-SH3 functions) with C287 capture for irreversible, sustained target engagement and pathway shutdown; the most differentiated route if achievable.

Covalent degrader anchor — use C287 as a covalent ligation point (or a high-occupancy covalent binder) to nucleate a YES1 PROTAC/molecular glue, degrading scaffolding function that catalytic inhibition leaves intact; SFK PROTACs already degrade SRC/Yes/Fyn/Fgr (e.g. DMP11), so the modality is feasible but currently non-selective.
deep.validation: STRONG genetic + emerging clinical validation. YES1 is a bona fide amplification-driven oncogene: focal 18p11.32 amplification/overexpression in lung adenocarcinoma & squamous, esophageal squamous (ESCC), TNBC, and mesothelioma; CRISPR/shRNA dependency demonstrated in YES1-amplified models; driver of acquired resistance to EGFR (PNAS 2018 transposon screen), ALK, and HER2/T-DM1 therapy (Cancer Discov / Nat-level reports). Clinical de-risking: (1) dasatinib produced a 69% target-lesion reduction in a YES1-amplified stage-IV lung adenocarcinoma patient; (2) NXP900 (Nuvectis), a YES1/SRC inhibitor, was biologically active with acceptable safety in its first-in-human Phase 1 (AACR 2025, CT153) — direct clinical proof the YES1/SFK node is druggable and tolerable. Modality (ATP-competitive kinase inhibition of an SFK) is among the most clinically validated in oncology.
deep.existing_covalent: Covalent lane is largely UNCLAIMED for YES1-selective agents but heavily shadowed. (1) DGY-06-116 (Gray/Dana-Farber, J Med Chem 2020; PDB 6E6E) — irreversible acrylamide on the SRC P-loop Cys277; SRC-DIRECTED tool compound, YES1 is a potent low-nM OFF-target, never advanced clinically. (2) SM1-71 (Cell Chem Biol 2019) — promiscuous acrylamide probe, covalently labels YES1 C287 but hits 20+ kinases; a probe, not a drug. (3) Futibatinib (approved FGFR inhibitor) — covalently hits SRC/YES off-target, i.e. validates the chemistry but as a liability. The clinical YES1 leader, NXP900/eCF506 (Nuvectis, Phase 1), is NON-covalent (reversible Type 1.5). No disclosed company program is running a YES1-SELECTIVE covalent inhibitor. So the covalent-selective lane is OPEN, but contested by a clinically-advanced reversible competitor and crowded with SRC-directed covalent chemistry that would need re-vectoring.
key_risks: SELECTIVITY vs SRC/FGR is the program-defining risk: C287 is shared with SRC C277 (near-identical pocket) and FGR, so the covalent warhead provides ZERO discrimination among these three — every gram of selectivity must come from the reversible scaffold, and pan-SFK (SRC) inhibition carries known tolerability/scaffolding-tox baggage. A 'YES1-selective covalent' may be chemically very hard to separate from SRC.

Differentiation vs incumbents: NXP900 already delivers sub-nM YES1 potency + dual catalytic/scaffolding blockade reversibly and is in Phase 1; a covalent entrant must prove that irreversible engagement buys real benefit (durability, lower dose, resistance-mutation coverage) over a clinically de-risked reversible Type 1.5 drug — otherwise it is a me-too behind a moving competitor.

Reactivity/geometry risk: C287 is a conditionally reactive P-loop cysteine requiring loop motion (slow k_inact), so a poorly vectored warhead gives weak covalent occupancy; plus P-loop/gatekeeper (Thr→Ile/Met) resistance mutations could blunt both binding and capture.
deep.first_experiment: Synthesize a small set of acrylamide analogs built on a YES1-biased reversible scaffold and run a head-to-head intact-protein LC/MS covalent-occupancy + NanoBRET target-engagement panel across the three shared-cysteine paralogs — YES1 (C287), SRC (C277), FGR — measuring k_inact/K_I for each. The single decisive readout: can ANY chemotype achieve >10x covalent-engagement selectivity for YES1 over SRC? If yes, the differentiated covalent program is real; if no (selectivity collapses onto SRC, as the DGY-06-116/futibatinib precedents predict), the honest play is pan-SRC/YES covalent or a covalent degrader, not 'YES1-selective covalent.' Pair with a C287S YES1 mutant to confirm the adduct site.

deep.covalent_handle: Cys298 — confirmed as the operative residue (the prior note is correct). It sits on the EDGE of the active site, near the nicotinamide ring of the NADPH cofactor (~3.9 Å van der Waals contact with C4/C5 of nicotinamide), at the mouth of the catalytic anion pocket (Tyr48/His110/Trp111) and adjacent to the inducible "specificity pocket" (loop C: Cys298-Ala299-Leu300-Leu301-Ser302-Tyr309). It is surface-accessible, NOT a hinge/P-loop/allosteric residue — it is an active-site-rim nucleophile. Reactivity is real and well documented: measured pKa ~8.4 (depressed for a Cys), and it is a genuinely hyper-reactive thiol — endogenously S-nitrosylated (DEA-NO), glutathiolated by GSSG, and oxidized to sulfenic acid in air, all at Cys298 specifically. This is a directed-electrophile-ready handle (Michael acceptors documented to add), not merely a scout-fragment hit. CRITICAL caveat: it is NOT cleanly ligandable in the holoenzyme — bound NADP(H) sterically shields Cys298 (it is the only Cys close enough to the cofactor to be protected), so in cells the cofactor-loaded enzyme blunts labeling. Two other active-site cysteines (Cys80, Cys303) add off-handle reactivity.
deep.handle_source: Literature site-directed mutagenesis (Cys298Ser, Petrash/Bhatnagar) + protein-biochemistry of endogenous covalent PTMs (S-nitrosylation, glutathiolation, sulfenylation at Cys298) + crystallography. PDB: 4JIR/8FH6 (AKR1B1 + NADP+ + epalrestat / AT-001), porcine AR sorbinil/tolrestat "specificity pocket" structures (PDB 2FZD class); AKR1B10 sulfenylated-Cys299 epalrestat structure PDB 4JIH. Reactivity is structure- and mutagenesis-grounded, not a chemoproteomic scout-fragment call (Cys298 is not a flagged hit in generic isoTOP-ABPP/CysDB scans, consistent with NADPH shielding in lysate).
deep.selectivity: SELECTIVITY LIABILITY at the residue level. Cys298 is CONSERVED across the human AKR1B subfamily and "many members" of the broader AKR superfamily. Aligned paralogs at the equivalent position: AKR1B10 = Cys299 (and it IS covalently modified there by PGA1); AKR1B15 = cysteine retained (AKR1B15 shares 68% identity with AKR1B1, 91% with AKR1B10). The subfamily shares 71% sequence identity. So a bare warhead pointed at Cys298 would be expected to also hit AKR1B10/AKR1B15 — a problem because AKR1B10 has its own (oncology) biology. The PARTIAL rescue: selectivity is achievable not from the Cys itself but from the surrounding pocket, which genuinely diverges — Trp112 (B10) vs Trp111 conformation, a flipped vs native rotamer stabilized by Gln114–Ser304 H-bonding, greater loop-A mobility and a "loop-A subpocket" in B10, and divergent residues at positions 301/303. This is exactly how PGA1 reaches Cys299 in B10 but NOT Cys298 in B1 — proof the same nucleophile can be discriminated by reversible-recognition framing. Net: the warhead is non-selective; selectivity must come entirely from the non-covalent scaffold, and the family is close enough that this is hard.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric covalent inhibition — the only well-supported route: a reversible ARI scaffold (anion-pocket binder, e.g. epalrestat/sorbinil chemotype) tethered to a Cys298-directed electrophile, locking the active site. Michael-acceptor addition to Cys298 is structurally demonstrated (PGA1 analog chemistry). Caveat: a covalent modifier of Cys298 can ACTIVATE the enzyme (C298S mimics activated AR; GSSG-glutathiolation inactivates, NO-nitrosylation activates) — so warhead chemistry must inhibit, not phenocopy the activating PTM.
Allosteric/interface/dimer trap — NOT viable: AKR1B1 is a monomeric (β/α)8-TIM-barrel with no validated allosteric or dimer-interface cysteine handle.

Degrader anchor — theoretically possible (Cys298 as a covalent attachment point for a PROTAC/molecular glue), but there is no validated degradation rationale and the cytosolic, abundant, cofactor-shielded enzyme is an unfavorable degrader substrate; speculative.
deep.validation: Target biology is heavily studied but the modality is NEGATIVELY de-risked. AKR1B1/polyol pathway is mechanistically validated in diabetic complications (sorbitol/galactitol accumulation), and govorestat shows clean target engagement (galactitol lowering). BUT the clinical track record is a graveyard: decades of reversible ARIs failed or were withdrawn (tolrestat withdrawn, zopolrestat, ranirestat, fidarestat stalled; epalrestat approved only in Japan/China for diabetic neuropathy). Most decisive recent reads: Applied Therapeutics AT-001/caficrestat MISSED the primary endpoint in the Phase 3 ARISE-HF diabetic-cardiomyopathy trial (topline Jan 2024), and govorestat received an FDA Complete Response Letter for Classic Galactosemia (Nov 27 2024). So the target is well-validated biochemically but the therapeutic hypothesis has repeatedly failed in registrational trials — a covalent inhibitor inherits that efficacy risk and adds it to the polyol pathway's known on-target liability (over-inhibition / activated-AR concerns).
deep.existing_covalent: No dedicated AKR1B1 (aldose reductase) covalent small-molecule program found — all clinical/advanced AKR1B1 inhibitors are REVERSIBLE competitive ARIs (epalrestat [approved JP/CN]; Applied Therapeutics AT-001/caficrestat, Phase 3 ARISE-HF, failed primary endpoint Jan 2024; govorestat/AT-007, FDA CRL Nov 2024; historical: tolrestat, zopolrestat, ranirestat, fidarestat, sorbinil). The ONLY covalent chemistry on this enzyme family is on the PARALOG AKR1B10 (oncology): cyclopentenone prostaglandin A1 (PGA1) forms a Michael adduct at AKR1B10-Cys299 (del Corral/Pérez-Sala, Cancer Res 2011; IC50 ~38 µM, GSH-reversible) — and PGA1 is reported AKR1B10-SELECTIVE, i.e. it does not efficiently hit AKR1B1-Cys298. So the covalent lane on AKR1B1 itself is unworked.
key_risks: EFFICACY / VALIDATION RISK (dominant): the reversible-ARI hypothesis has repeatedly failed in registrational trials (AT-001 missed ARISE-HF Phase 3 Jan 2024; govorestat FDA CRL Nov 2024; multiple prior ARI withdrawals). A covalent AR inhibitor competes in a clinically de-risked-DOWN space — being 'better at inhibiting AR' may not translate to benefit, and a best-in-class covalent asset against a target whose biology keeps failing is a weak BIC thesis.

SELECTIVITY RISK: Cys298 is conserved across AKR1B10/AKR1B15 and broadly in the AKR superfamily, so the warhead is intrinsically non-selective; selectivity must be engineered entirely from the non-covalent scaffold against >70%-identical paralogs (notably oncogenic AKR1B10) — and a covalent off-target adduct is permanent. On-target risk is also real: covalent modification of Cys298 can ACTIVATE AR (phenocopying the activating S-nitrosylation), so the wrong chemistry worsens disease.

CELLULAR TRACTABILITY RISK: NADP(H) shields Cys298 in the holoenzyme (the cofactor is bound at high cellular occupancy in this abundant cytosolic enzyme), blunting covalent engagement in cells; combined with competing reactivity at Cys80/Cys303 and the buried-cleft geometry, achieving high cellular covalent occupancy may be hard.
deep.first_experiment: Intact-protein LC-MS covalent-engagement triage with the cofactor as the gating variable: incubate recombinant AKR1B1 holoenzyme (+NADP+) vs apoenzyme (−cofactor) with a small panel of epalrestat/sorbinil-scaffold–tethered Michael acceptors, and measure stoichiometry/kinetics (kinact/Ki) of Cys298 adduction by deconvoluted intact MS + tryptic-peptide MS/MS to localize the adduct to Cys298 (not Cys80/Cys303). This single experiment decides the program: it answers (a) can a directed electrophile covalently and site-specifically hit Cys298 at all, and (b) does physiological NADP(H) occupancy abolish that engagement — the make-or-break tractability question. Run a Cys298Ser mutant and AKR1B10 in parallel as the selectivity counter-screen. If engagement survives the +NADP+ condition AND is lost on C298S AND is weak on AKR1B10, the handle is real and selective; if NADP+ blocks it, the covalent thesis is dead regardless of validation.

deep.covalent_handle: No tractable orthosteric covalent handle. Direct parsing of the UniProt sequence (P05129, 697 aa) shows the kinase domain (351-614) contains exactly FOUR cysteines, all in regulatory/structurally-constrained positions, none in the front pocket/hinge where covalent kinase inhibitors normally engage: (1) Cys502 = DFG+1 ("ITDFGMCK"), buried in the regulatory spine, conformationally gated by DFG-in/out; (2) Cys516 = activation-loop ("TTRTFCGTPDY", immediately N-terminal to the APE motif), solvent-exposed but highly mobile/disordered when unphosphorylated; (3) Cys395 = beta3/VAIK region ("QDDDVDCTLVEK"), partially buried; (4) Cys586 = alphaF helix ("REAVAICKG"), largely buried/structural. Plus Cys636 in the AGC C-tail (FRPRPC), distal to the ATP site. The cysteine-RICH part of PKCgamma is the N-terminal C1A/C1B domains (C20,49,52,66,69,77,85,114,117,131,133,134,142,150), but those are zinc-coordinating structural thiols, not ligandable. The "putative gamma-unique cysteine" in the prior handle note is NOT supported by the sequence. pKa/reactivity unmeasured; Cys516 (A-loop) is the only solvent-accessible candidate and would require a directed electrophile, not scout-fragment-detected here.
deep.handle_source: Structure/sequence (UniProt P05129 parsed directly; cysteine positions verified by counting, correcting two erroneous LLM extractions). PKC catalytic-domain structural reference = PKCbetaII (PDB 2I0E, catalytic domain + bisindolylmaleimide, Grodsky 2006; full-length 4.0A). No PKCgamma kinase-domain crystal structure exists in the PDB. No CysDB/isoTOP-ABPP entry confirming reactivity of any PKCgamma kinase cysteine was found; the only PKC ABPP precedent is DMF hitting a regulatory (non-catalytic) cysteine in PKCtheta.
deep.selectivity: DECISIVE NEGATIVE. Every kinase-domain cysteine is CONSERVED across the PKC family, making any warhead a pan-PKC liability rather than a gamma handle. Aligned paralog residues at each position: Cys502 (DFG+1) -> Cys in PKCalpha (P17252, "ADFGMCKEH"), PKCbeta (P05771, "ADFGMCKEN"), PKCdelta, PKCepsilon, PKCeta - a pan-cPKC/nPKC signature residue. Cys516 (activation loop, "TFCGTPDY") -> Cys in PKCalpha, PKCbeta, PKCdelta, PKCepsilon - pan-PKC. Cys395 (beta3) -> Cys in PKCalpha/beta ("DDDVECTM") and PKCdelta/epsilon/eta - pan-PKC. Cys586 (alphaF) -> Cys in PKCalpha ("EAVSVCKG") and PKCbeta ("EAVAICKG") - conventional-PKC conserved. Conclusion: there is NO unique-to-gamma cysteine in the catalytic domain; closest paralogs PKCalpha and PKCbeta share all four. A covalent warhead at any would also hit the broadly-expressed, tumor-suppressive PKCalpha/beta - a serious tox/selectivity risk.
mechanism_routes: Orthosteric covalent inhibition: NOT viable as a selective handle - the only A-loop/DFG cysteines are pan-PKC conserved; achieving gamma-selectivity would have to come entirely from the reversible recognition element, not the warhead. Reversible ATP-competitive PKC inhibitors already fail isoform selectivity.

Allosteric / C1-C2 regulatory-domain or autoinhibition-stabilizing covalent: most disease-relevant route (SCA14 is driven by impaired autoinhibition). Regulatory-domain cysteines exist but are zinc-structural in C1; a covalent ligand that re-clamps the pseudosubstrate/C1-kinase interface is conceptually attractive but unprecedented and unmapped. Highest scientific novelty, highest risk.

Degrader anchor: a covalent ligand (even non-selective, at e.g. Cys516) could serve as a TPD warhead where degradation selectivity is shaped by ternary-complex/E3 geometry rather than warhead selectivity; viable in principle but no PKCgamma degrader exists and brain delivery of a bifunctional is hard.
deep.validation: Genetic validation is STRONG and direction-clarified: SCA14 is caused by PRKCG missense mutations that impair autoinhibition and degradation, producing leaky GAIN of PKCgamma activity (Newton lab, basal activity inversely correlates with age of onset) - so INHIBITION is the correct direction for SCA14 and for neuropathic pain (PKCgamma-KO mice show reduced neuropathic pain). Brain/spinal-cord-restricted, neuron-specific expression (notably Purkinje cells) - clean for CNS-only pharmacology but mandates BBB penetrance. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: in cancer, conventional PKCs (incl. PKCgamma) behave largely as TUMOR SUPPRESSORS (cancer mutations are predominantly loss-of-function), so chronic systemic pan-PKC inhibition is mechanistically contraindicated - reinforcing that a pan-PKC warhead is dangerous. Clinical de-risking of the MODALITY (covalent) is high generally, but ZERO clinical de-risking for covalent or even selective PKCgamma inhibition specifically. No approved or clinical PKCgamma-selective agent exists.
deep.existing_covalent: No PKCgamma-selective covalent program found (search "PRKCG covalent inhibitor" returns none). The entire clinical PKC landscape is reversible ATP-competitive: midostaurin (PKC329/staurosporine analog, approved for FLT3 AML - pan-kinase), sotrastaurin/AEB071 (pan-cPKC/nPKC, Novartis, transplant/psoriasis - discontinued), enzastaurin (PKCbeta-pref, Eli Lilly - failed Phase III glioma/DLBCL), ruboxistaurin (PKCbeta), bryostatin (modulator, not inhibitor). The ONLY covalent PKC precedent is dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera) covalently modifying conserved REGULATORY-domain (non-catalytic) cysteines in PKCtheta - non-selective, repurposed observation, not a designed gamma program. Net: covalent PKCgamma lane is OPEN, but open because no one has found a selective tractable handle, not because of an obvious opening.
key_risks: SELECTIVITY (fatal as currently framed): all four catalytic-domain cysteines are pan-PKC conserved (shared with tumor-suppressive PKCalpha/beta); the prior 'gamma-unique cysteine' premise is false. A warhead provides no gamma discrimination; selectivity must come entirely from reversible recognition, where decades of ATP-competitive PKC chemistry have largely failed to separate isoforms.

MODALITY/INDICATION mismatch: cPKCs are tumor suppressors in cancer (loss-of-function mutations dominate), so systemic chronic pan-PKC covalent inhibition risks tumor promotion; the only clean inhibition indications (SCA14, neuropathic pain) are CNS and demand a brain-penetrant covalent agent - a hard combination.

NO STRUCTURE + NO REACTIVITY DATA: no PKCgamma kinase-domain crystal structure, and no chemoproteomic evidence that Cys516 (the lone accessible A-loop cysteine) is actually reactive/ligandable; the A-loop is mobile and only ordered when phosphorylated, so engageability is unproven.
deep.first_experiment: Run reactive-cysteine chemoproteomics (isoTOP-ABPP / scout-fragment competition, e.g. iodoacetamide-alkyne +/- a broad acrylamide fragment) on recombinant active PKCgamma kinase domain AND in neuronal lysate, with a parallel PKCalpha/PKCbeta panel, to answer the single decisive question: is Cys516 (or Cys502/Cys586) actually liganded by a covalent fragment, and if so is the labeling stoichiometry/ratio ANY different between PKCgamma and PKCalpha/beta? If no cysteine is engaged, or engagement is identical across cPKCs (the expected result given conservation), the covalent orthosteric thesis is dead and effort should pivot to a non-cysteine modality. This costs little and kills or validates the program in one experiment.
